newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin recovering, but illness serious-doctors.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin recovering, but illness serious-doctors.

text.p: Doctors said on Wednesday that President Boris Yeltsin was recovering after a week in hospital with pneumonia, but warned that the illness was serious and complications were possible.
Kremlin chief doctor Sergei Mironov said Yeltsin should stay in hospital this week. "Beyond that it will depend on the course of his illness."
Yeltsin, 65, was taken to hospital last Wednesday with pneumonia, although doctors have said the ailment is not linked to heart problems the Russian leader suffered in 1995 and 1996.
They said on Friday he would spend just three days in hospital, but the stay has already been prolonged.
Yeltsin underwent a quintuple heart bypass operation on November 5 after his third heart attack, which took place just before the second round of the Russian presidential election.
He has spent only a few days in the Kremlin since the poll, which took place on July 3.

Mironov said Yeltsin had become more active in the last few days, although doctors were trying to limit his movements. But Yeltsin's case of double pneumonia, which affects both lungs, should not be taken lightly.
"I should say that this is a fairly serious illness, which of course brings with it a whole range of possible complications," he added. "In this respect, there will be a daily doctors' meeting."

He said doctors still assumed that the president would be able to attend a meeting of the heads of government of the Commonwealth of Independent States, due to take place in Moscow towards the end of January.
"We are counting on Boris Nikolayevich taking part in these events," Mironov said.
He said Yeltsin had probably caught a cold after taking a Russian banya -- a traditional steam bath -- and that this had developed into bronchitis and then pneumonia.

Opposition deputies in the communist-dominated State Duma lower house of parliament have began discussing if Yeltsin's prolonged illness would give them grounds to remove him from office, although they admit there is little chance of success.
Mironov, referring to Russian labour law which counts a period of sickness from the date when an invalid last worked said that Yeltsin had officially only been out of the Kremlin for a week.
